en: Three command capabilities, all of them about executions or peers. The lifecycle transitions exist only in lib/plan.sh and lib/start.sh. `majordomus run` executes in its own process and never reaches the running server, so the execution plane the Cockpit shows and the one a person uses are disjoint. A server whose executable has been replaced still reports itself `ready`. Two capabilities — devtask.issue and devtask.milestone — landed after the audit's base and give the runtime its first canonical read of an issue and a milestone as work; neither of them writes anything.
cs: Tři příkazové schopnosti, všechny o exekucích nebo peerech. Přechody životního cyklu existují jen v lib/plan.sh a lib/start.sh. `majordomus run` se provádí ve vlastním procesu a nikdy nedosáhne běžícího serveru, takže rovina exekucí, kterou ukazuje Cockpit, a ta, kterou používá člověk, jsou disjunktní. Server, jehož spustitelný soubor byl nahrazen, se stále hlásí jako `ready`. Dvě schopnosti — devtask.issue a devtask.milestone — přistály po základu auditu a dávají runtime první kanonické čtení úkolu a milníku jako práce; ani jedna nic nezapisuje.

en: The two formats exist because one file cannot be both things. The record is what the provider sent and what everything else is derived from; escaped, on one line, it is not what a person opens. The rendering is what a person opens; decoded and reflowed, it is not what a byte-faithful archive can be rebuilt from. Keeping only one would either give up the evidence or give up the reading, so both are written on every capture, and the asymmetry between them is what makes the pair enforceable: <t1/> can rebuild any rendering from its record, and nothing can go the other way. <t2/> therefore fails on a record with no rendering and names <t3/> as the repair, and fails on a rendering with no record while offering none, because that half is unrecoverable and only a person should decide to delete it.

Vykreslení je to, co člověk otevírá; dekódované a přeformátované není tím, z čeho lze znovu sestavit bajtově věrný archiv. Ponechat jen jedno by buď vzdalo důkaz, nebo čtení, takže se při každém zachycení zapisují obě a asymetrie mezi nimi je to, co z dvojice činí vynutitelnou: <t1/> umí z jeho záznamu znovu sestavit jakékoli vykreslení, ale opačně nic. <t2/> proto selže na záznamu bez vykreslení a jmenuje <t3/> jako nápravu a selže na vykreslení bez záznamu, aniž nabídne nápravu, protože ta polovina je nezotavitelná a smazat ji smí rozhodnout jen člověk.

en: <t1/> <t2>Reads what the runs already wrote — the suite's TSV report, cargo test's output, a coverage summary — carries into each result what that run measured about its own checkout (the commit and the tree, from the measurement `evidence stamp` wrote), with the digest of the test's own source, the time and the origin, and merges it into the ledger. It records; it decides nothing: a case that failed is a case the runner said failed, and a test no report named is left exactly as it was, so recording one case never erases the evidence for the rest. It refuses a tree with no commit, a measurement of another commit or of another report, a local measurement that names no report, and a CI report without a measurement; a local report recorded without one carries the tree unknown, which never reads proven. Every recording returns a run record (its commit, the tree each report's run measured, its totals and what was absent, dropped or unknown, and a coverage summary bound to its commit), and --ledger local writes only the ignored local ledger. A crate binary that ran no test, or only a filtered subset, is recorded as a skip, and what no claim can name yet (the crate's own unit tests, its doctests) is listed as dropped.</t2> <t3> <t4>command</t4> <t5>behaviorally_verified</t5> <t6>cli</t6> </t3>

The mapping from a module to its page is the check's own: <t3/> keeps the modules the crate exports and derives each one's page from the crate's inventory — the routes the report lists under <t4/>, each of which the check requires of the tree — and <t5/> carries that answer into the site's registry dataset as <t6/> on each module (the surface, the module's crate path, the page within the surface). A module rustdoc gives no page, one declared <t7/> or private, carries none, so no link is made that could answer <t8/>. The template derives no route: it joins that field with the surfaces the build composed, which <t9/> records with their mounts in <t10/>, and links through <t11/> at the mount the build composed the reference at. A build whose topology lacks the reference, or a plain <t12/> with no <t13/>, links nothing. The Cockpit's module pages are a separate renderer and are not covered here.

en: A distribution model is the textbook shape of the failure this repository exists to catch. The same fact — that a platform is supported — has to be true in the release build matrix, in the installer's target table, in the documentation's platform table, on the website, and in whatever the tool says about itself. Written down five times it is wrong within a release: the tag builds five artifacts and the installer offers six, or the documentation promises a platform nothing built, and the failure is discovered by a person who cannot install the tool.
cs: Distribuční model je učebnicový tvar selhání, které tento repozitář existuje, aby zachytil. Týž fakt — že platforma je podporována — musí platit v matici release buildu, v cílové tabulce instalátoru, v tabulce platforem v dokumentaci, na webu a ve všem, co nástroj říká sám o sobě. Zapsaný pětkrát je do jednoho release nesprávný: tag sestaví pět artefaktů a instalátor nabízí šest, nebo dokumentace slibuje platformu, kterou nic nesestavilo, a selhání objeví člověk, který nástroj nemůže nainstalovat.
